```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Load in necessary libraries and dataset
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(StMoMo)
library(demography)
library(arrow)
```

```{r dataset}
deaths <- read.table("/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/Deaths_1x1.txt", skip = 2, header = TRUE, na.strings = ".")
expo   <- read.table("/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/Exposures_1x1.txt", skip = 2, header = TRUE, na.strings = ".")
```

Only look at age 30-100 and year 1990-2023
```{r age and year filtering}
deaths$Age <- as.numeric(sub("\\+", "", deaths$Age))
deaths <- deaths[deaths$Year >= 1990 & deaths$Age >= 30 & deaths$Age <= 100, ]
expo$Age <- as.numeric(sub("\\+", "", expo$Age))
expo <- expo[expo$Year >= 1990 & expo$Age >= 30 & expo$Age <= 100, ]
```

Create death rates and plot for male and female separately
```{r}
# Long format: one row per Year, Age, Sex
deaths_long <- deaths %>%
  select(Year, Age, Female, Male) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Female, Male), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "Deaths")

expo_long <- expo %>%
  select(Year, Age, Female, Male) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Female, Male), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "Exposure")

# Join and compute death rates
rates <- deaths_long %>%
  left_join(expo_long, by = c("Year", "Age", "Sex")) %>%
  mutate(m = Deaths / Exposure,
         log_m = log(m))

# Plot log death rate over time for selected ages, one panel per sex
rates %>%
  filter(Age %in% c(30, 50, 65, 80, 95)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = log_m, colour = factor(Age))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "log death rate", colour = "Age",
       title = "Log death rates in the Netherlands, 1990-2023") +
  theme_minimal()
```
## MALES

Fit Lee-carter model
```{r turn data into matrices}
# Turn long data into age x year matrices for one sex
make_matrix <- function(df, sex, var) {
  df %>%
    filter(Sex == sex) %>%
    select(Age, Year, all_of(var)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = all_of(var)) %>%
    arrange(Age) %>%
    select(-Age) %>%
    as.matrix()
}

ages  <- sort(unique(rates$Age))
years <- sort(unique(rates$Year))

Dxt_m <- make_matrix(rates, "Male", "Deaths")
Ext_m <- make_matrix(rates, "Male", "Exposure")
dimnames(Dxt_m) <- dimnames(Ext_m) <- list(ages, years)

Dxt_f <- make_matrix(rates, "Female", "Deaths")
Ext_f <- make_matrix(rates, "Female", "Exposure")
dimnames(Dxt_f) <- dimnames(Ext_f) <- list(ages, years)

```

```{r fit lee-carter model to male data}
# Lee-Carter with Poisson errors and log link (central exposures)
LC <- lc(link = "log")

LCfit_m <- fit(LC, Dxt = Dxt_m, Ext = Ext_m, ages = ages, years = years)

# Quick checks
plot(LCfit_m)                        # a_x, b_x, k_t
res_m <- residuals(LCfit_m)
plot(res_m, type = "colourmap")      # residual heatmap
```

try to get rid of the clear bands of the cohorts by using Renshaw-Haberman
```{r}
# Give zero weight to cohorts with fewer than 3 observations (corners of the data)
wxt <- genWeightMat(ages = ages, years = years, clip = 3)

# Refit LC with the same weights so the comparison is fair
LCfit_m <- fit(LC, Dxt = Dxt_m, Ext = Ext_m, ages = ages, years = years, wxt = wxt)

# Renshaw-Haberman: log m = a_x + b_x k_t + g_(t-x)
RH <- rh(link = "log", cohortAgeFun = "1")
RHfit_m <- fit(RH, Dxt = Dxt_m, Ext = Ext_m, ages = ages, years = years, wxt = wxt,
               start.ax = LCfit_m$ax, start.bx = LCfit_m$bx, start.kt = LCfit_m$kt, itermax = 10000)

plot(RHfit_m, parametricbx = FALSE)   # check that the cohort effect g_c looks sensible

# Residuals side by side, same colour scale
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(residuals(LCfit_m), type = "colourmap", reslim = c(-3.5, 3.5), main = "Lee-Carter")
plot(residuals(RHfit_m), type = "colourmap", reslim = c(-3.5, 3.5), main = "Renshaw-Haberman")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Information criteria (lower is better)
data.frame(model = c("LC", "RH"),
           loglik = c(LCfit_m$loglik, RHfit_m$loglik),
           npar = c(LCfit_m$npar, RHfit_m$npar),
           AIC = c(AIC(LCfit_m), AIC(RHfit_m)),
           BIC = c(BIC(LCfit_m), BIC(RHfit_m)))
```

next step is to forecast now that the bands are gone. Check whether LC or RH gives more meaningful results in forecasting.
```{r}
h <- 50          # forecast horizon in years
nsim <- 1000     # number of simulated scenarios

# Central forecasts (random walk with drift for k_t, ARIMA(1,1,0) for the cohort effect)
LCfor_m <- forecast(LCfit_m, h = h)
RHfor_m <- forecast(RHfit_m, h = h, gc.order = c(1, 1, 0))

plot(LCfor_m, only.kt = TRUE)
plot(RHfor_m)                    # k_t and gamma forecasts

# Stochastic scenarios
set.seed(1)
LCsim_m <- simulate(LCfit_m, nsim = nsim, h = h)
RHsim_m <- simulate(RHfit_m, nsim = nsim, h = h, gc.order = c(1, 1, 0))

# Period life expectancy at 65 from a vector of death rates named by age
e_x <- function(m, from_age = 65) {
  m <- m[as.numeric(names(m)) >= from_age]
  sum(cumprod(exp(-m))) + 0.5
}

# Central forecast: e65 per year
e65_LC <- apply(LCfor_m$rates, 2, e_x)
e65_RH <- apply(RHfor_m$rates, 2, e_x)

# Simulations: e65 per year per scenario, then 2.5% / 50% / 97.5% quantiles
e65_LC_sim <- apply(LCsim_m$rates, c(2, 3), e_x)
e65_RH_sim <- apply(RHsim_m$rates, c(2, 3), e_x)
q_LC <- apply(e65_LC_sim, 1, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
q_RH <- apply(e65_RH_sim, 1, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))

# Plot both models with 95% bands
yrs <- as.numeric(colnames(q_LC))
plot(yrs, q_LC[2, ], type = "l", col = "blue",
     ylim = range(q_LC, q_RH), xlab = "Year", ylab = "Period e65",
     main = "Projected life expectancy at 65 (men)")
lines(yrs, q_LC[1, ], lty = 2, col = "blue"); lines(yrs, q_LC[3, ], lty = 2, col = "blue")
lines(yrs, q_RH[2, ], col = "red")
lines(yrs, q_RH[1, ], lty = 2, col = "red"); lines(yrs, q_RH[3, ], lty = 2, col = "red")
legend("topleft", c("LC", "RH"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1)

# Comparison in 2050
rbind(LC = q_LC[, "2050"], RH = q_RH[, "2050"])
```

RH fits better (AIC/BIC, residuals), but its forecasts are unstable because of the trade-off between period and cohort trends.
LC is therefore chosen for projection, with its known weakness (no cohort effect) mentioned.

## FEMALES

Fit Lee-carter model

```{r fit lee-carter model to female data}
# Lee-Carter with Poisson errors and log link (central exposures)
LC <- lc(link = "log")

LCfit_f <- fit(LC, Dxt = Dxt_f, Ext = Ext_f, ages = ages, years = years)

# Quick checks
plot(LCfit_f)                        # a_x, b_x, k_t
res_f <- residuals(LCfit_f)
plot(res_f, type = "colourmap")      # residual heatmap
```



try to get rid of the clear bands of the cohorts by using Renshaw-Haberman
```{r}
# Give zero weight to cohorts with fewer than 3 observations (corners of the data)
wxt <- genWeightMat(ages = ages, years = years, clip = 3)

# Refit LC with the same weights so the comparison is fair
LCfit_f <- fit(LC, Dxt = Dxt_f, Ext = Ext_f, ages = ages, years = years, wxt = wxt)

# Renshaw-Haberman: log m = a_x + b_x k_t + g_(t-x)
RH <- rh(link = "log", cohortAgeFun = "1")
RHfit_f <- fit(RH, Dxt = Dxt_f, Ext = Ext_f, ages = ages, years = years, wxt = wxt,
               start.ax = LCfit_f$ax, start.bx = LCfit_f$bx, start.kt = LCfit_f$kt, itermax = 10000)

plot(RHfit_f, parametricbx = FALSE)   # check that the cohort effect g_c looks sensible

# Residuals side by side, same colour scale
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(residuals(LCfit_f), type = "colourmap", reslim = c(-3.5, 3.5), main = "Lee-Carter")
plot(residuals(RHfit_f), type = "colourmap", reslim = c(-3.5, 3.5), main = "Renshaw-Haberman")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Information criteria (lower is better)
data.frame(model = c("LC", "RH"),
           loglik = c(LCfit_f$loglik, RHfit_f$loglik),
           npar = c(LCfit_f$npar, RHfit_f$npar),
           AIC = c(AIC(LCfit_f), AIC(RHfit_f)),
           BIC = c(BIC(LCfit_f), BIC(RHfit_f)))
```

next step is to forecast now that the bands are gone. Check whether LC or RH gives more meaningful results in forecasting.
```{r}
h <- 50          # forecast horizon in years
nsim <- 1000     # number of simulated scenarios

# Central forecasts (random walk with drift for k_t, ARIMA(1,1,0) for the cohort effect)

plot(LCfor_f, only.kt = TRUE)
plot(RHfor_f)                    # k_t and gamma forecasts

# Stochastic scenarios

LCsim_f <- simulate(LCfit_f, nsim = nsim, h = h)
RHsim_f <- simulate(RHfit_f, nsim = nsim, h = h, gc.order = c(1, 1, 0))

# Period life expectancy at 65 from a vector of death rates named by age
e_x <- function(m, from_age = 65) {
  m <- m[as.numeric(names(m)) >= from_age]
  sum(cumprod(exp(-m))) + 0.5
}

# Central forecast: e65 per year
e65_LC <- apply(LCfor_f$rates, 2, e_x)
e65_RH <- apply(RHfor_f$rates, 2, e_x)

# Simulations: e65 per year per scenario, then 2.5% / 50% / 97.5% quantiles
e65_LC_sim <- apply(LCsim_f$rates, c(2, 3), e_x)
e65_RH_sim <- apply(RHsim_f$rates, c(2, 3), e_x)
q_LC <- apply(e65_LC_sim, 1, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
q_RH <- apply(e65_RH_sim, 1, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))

# Plot both models with 95% bands
yrs <- as.numeric(colnames(q_LC))
plot(yrs, q_LC[2, ], type = "l", col = "blue",

lines(yrs, q_LC[1, ], lty = 2, col = "blue"); lines(yrs, q_LC[3, ], lty = 2, col = "blue")
lines(yrs, q_RH[2, ], col = "red")

```

## Export to python

Export projected rates to python, create data files

```{r export male}
# Central forecast
central_m <- as.data.frame(as.table(LCfor_m$rates)) %>%
  setNames(c("Age", "Year", "m")) %>%
  mutate(Age = as.numeric(as.character(Age)),
         Year = as.numeric(as.character(Year)),
         Sex = "Male")

write.csv(central_m, "/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/central_rates_male.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Simulated scenarios
sims_m <- as.data.frame(as.table(LCsim_m$rates)) %>%
  setNames(c("Age", "Year", "Sim", "m")) %>%
  mutate(Age = as.numeric(as.character(Age)),
         Year = as.numeric(as.character(Year)),
         Sim = as.integer(Sim),
         Sex = "Male")

write_parquet(sims_m, "/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/sim_rates_male.parquet")
```

```{r export female}

central_f <- as.data.frame(as.table(LCfor_f$rates)) %>%

  mutate(Age = as.numeric(as.character(Age)),

write.csv(central_f, "/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/central_rates_female.csv", row.names = FALSE)

write_parquet(sims_f, "/Users/danielwolff/Actuary-project/data/sim_rates_female.parquet")
```
